name: Abijam
bio: Abijam (called Abijah throughout 2 Chronicles) was Rehoboam's son, who succeeded him as king of Judah after Rehoboam's seventeen-year reign ended and he was buried in the City of David (1 Kings 14:31). Of all his father's many children, Abijam was the one Rehoboam loved best, as the son of his favorite wife Maachah, daughter of Absalom; Rehoboam appointed him chief among his brothers and intended all along for him to be king (2 Chronicles 11:21-22). He reigned three years in Jerusalem; his mother was Maachah, daughter of Abishalom. Abijam committed all the sins his father had committed before him, and his heart was not fully devoted to the LORD as David's had been — yet for David's sake the LORD preserved a lamp for him in Jerusalem, raising up his son after him. There was war between Abijam and Jeroboam throughout his reign. When Abijam died, he was buried in the City of David, and his son Asa succeeded him (1 Kings 15:1-8).
